title: Choosing between Rc clone and make_mut
prompt: When should you use `Rc::make_mut` instead of explicitly cloning the inner value before mutating?
answer: `Rc::make_mut` provides copy-on-write behavior by checking the reference count at runtime. If the `Rc` has only one owner, `Rc::make_mut` gives mutable access to the existing allocation without cloning. It only clones the inner value when the pointer is actively shared with other handles.
